summary: Launch-week mix. Mostly open-source swaps for paid tools (voice, chat, search, images, clips), plus Omnisend's MCP, the ECC skills toolkit and small AI-product launches. Free coding routing (FreeLLMAPI) and ECC are the most useful for Claude Code.

tools.name: Pexo
tools.what: AI video agent that turns an idea into a product launch video.
tools.shown: Hosts discussed it and showed the site; no live build.
tools.quote: It's an AI video agent that turns your ideas into videos.
tools.check: Pricing not stated.

tools.name: Spira AI
tools.what: Platform that creates and runs a fake AI influencer account promoting your product.
tools.shown: Showed an example AI influencer promoting a brand; hosts did not try it.
tools.quote: you can now get your own fake influencer that's basically just promoting your stuff.
tools.check: 50% off offer claimed; Product Hunt number one claim not verified.

tools.name: ChatGPT Dots
tools.what: OpenAI agent that can manage Codex threads and ChatGPT chats from one place.
tools.shown: Corey described using it as a chief of staff to spin up and track Codex threads; Andrew found it nagging.
tools.quote: I use Dot as almost the manager of codec.
tools.check: Availability and price not stated.

tools.name: Hark
tools.what: New agent app with better web browser access and widgets that track your accounts.
tools.shown: Showed Alex Finn's screenshot of widgets; hosts were lukewarm and had not used it.
tools.quote: I don't see it being that unique enough for me to go and test it out
tools.check: Early access; price unknown.

tools.name: Claude for Startups
tools.what: Anthropic programme giving eligible startups a year of Claude for Teams and API credits.
tools.shown: Read out the offer; hosts said they are applying.
tools.quote: free access. One year of Claude for Teams, $1,000 in Claude API credits
tools.check: Eligibility (company 5 years or younger, or funded in last 2 years) as stated; check the page.

tools.name: Instinct
tools.what: Personal AI agent that lives in iMessage and just added group chats.
tools.shown: Corey described finding accountant documents in his email within about 60 seconds by text.
tools.quote: So, it has access to my email.
tools.check: Needs email and card access; check privacy. Price not stated.

tools.name: VMPal
tools.what: Mac app that runs isolated virtual machines so an agent gets its own computer.
tools.shown: Andrew explained plans to run a fresh Mac OS VM for agents; no demo.
tools.quote: if you're going to give your agent a computer, you might as well put it on your own computer and then isolate it to that one computer.
tools.check: One-off fee of about $34-35 claimed; Mac only as described.

tools.name: Boring Funnels
tools.what: Weekly full-funnel breakdowns plus a copy-able prompt for Claude Code or Codex to rebuild the funnel.
tools.shown: Described the product; no live use.
tools.quote: one-click prompt that you can one-click copy, hand to Claude Code, or hand to Codex
tools.check: Price said as '$2.99 a year' in captions; verify.

tools.name: Skillry
tools.what: Paid directory of premium agent skills with a visible demo of each output.
tools.shown: Showed the site, a pixel promo video skill demo and its verified revenue.
tools.quote: This is where you pay a smaller price for premium skills and you can see exactly what the output's going to look like before you buy it.
tools.check: $5,000 a month revenue claim via TrustMRR; skill price $4.99 as stated.

tools.name: CreativeClaw
tools.what: One MCP that adds image, video and voiceover generation to Claude, Codex and other agents, pay per use.
tools.shown: Showed example outputs and revenue page.
tools.quote: with one MCP, you get to make it into much more of an artist.
tools.check: Revenue figures ($10k MRR, $125k lifetime) are the founder's; verify.

tools.name: vibe-code.ing
tools.what: Clean single-page directory of AI tools, monetised by sponsored spots.
tools.shown: Showed the site as an example of a simple profitable idea.
tools.quote: this is just a really good example of a AI tool directory done right.
tools.check: Sponsored slot price stated as about $350.

tools.name: TinyPopups
tools.what: Embeddable website popup widget with triggers, installed in about five minutes.
tools.shown: Described the features and claimed reply rates; no demo.
tools.quote: intelligent website popups that take five it takes 5 minutes to install this on your website.
tools.check: 30% reply rate is the maker's claim.

tools.name: Omnisend MCP
tools.what: MCP that lets Claude or another agent build email campaigns and customer segments in Omnisend.
tools.shown: Live demo in Claude: campaign draft from top campaigns, new-subscriber segment, competitor style guide from Gmail, then a campaign.
tools.quote: Based on the best performing email campaigns, I want you to use Omnisend MCP to create an email campaign
tools.check: Sponsor link with 30% off; pricing and free tier not stated. Image upload through Claude failed in demo.

tools.name: VoiceStudio
tools.what: Free desktop app for voice cloning, text-to-speech and video dubbing, run locally.
tools.shown: Played sample voices and the install page.
tools.quote: There is no credit counter, so you can redo a line 50 times and it's going to cost you nothing.
tools.check: Default model is non-commercial only; Pro is $99 a month.

tools.name: Odysseus
tools.what: Private ChatGPT-style assistant on your computer with local models, memory, research and agents, made by PewDiePie.
tools.shown: Described features and the GitHub repo; no demo.
tools.quote: you're going to get chat, you're going to get deep research, you're going to get memory
tools.check: Host says it is not as good as ChatGPT.

tools.name: FreeLLMAPI
tools.what: Routes a coding agent across many free model providers so you can keep coding when one hits its limit.
tools.shown: Explained the idea and said the install is easy; no coding demo.
tools.quote: string together all these freebies
tools.check: Does not include Claude or frontier models; optional $19 a year add-on. Host frames it as replacing Claude Code for some people.

tools.name: Vane
tools.what: Self-hosted research assistant that searches the web and gives numbered sources; formerly Perplexica.
tools.shown: Described features; no demo.
tools.quote: You type a question. It searches the web. It writes the answer. It gives you numbered sources.
tools.check: Host says it is not as strong as Perplexity; needs a model (Ollama or free Gemini key).

tools.name: InvokeAI
tools.what: Open-source local image studio with layered canvas and editing.
tools.shown: Described features; no demo.
tools.quote: It's the AI image studio that you can run yourself.
tools.check: Needs a strong GPU or recent Mac.

tools.name: ACE-Step
tools.what: Open-source song generator with vocals that runs on your own computer.
tools.shown: Made a short hip-hop song on the hosted web version; host said it was not as good as Suno.
tools.quote: unlimited songs hosted by you for free.
tools.check: Quality below Suno per host.

tools.name: OpenShorts
tools.what: Self-hosted tool that turns long videos into captioned vertical clips and can schedule posts.
tools.shown: Ran it on a YouTube video on the free hosted site; framing needed fixing.
tools.quote: This is a free clip maker that you can host yourself or you can go to their website and use for free.
tools.check: Hosted free tier is 20 minutes a month with watermark; self-hosting slow without GPU.

tools.name: Dyad
tools.what: Open-source local app builder that turns plain English into apps using your chosen AI model.
tools.shown: Described features; no demo.
tools.quote: You just describe what you want in plain English and you get it.
tools.check: Model cost depends on what you plug in; free Gemini key possible.

tools.name: OpenManus
tools.what: Open-source general agent that plans, browses, codes and saves files using your own model.
tools.shown: Described features; no demo.
tools.quote: You type what you want, the goal in English, and it plans the steps itself.
tools.check: Needs a paid API key or limited free tier.

tools.name: Upscayl
tools.what: Free desktop app that upscales photos four times locally, singly or in bulk.
tools.shown: Showed the repo and described the models.
tools.quote: It runs on your computer so your photos never leave
tools.check: Needs a Vulkan-capable GPU.

tools.name: ECC
tools.what: Open-source toolkit of skills that plans, builds with tests, makes a promo video and sends outreach.
tools.shown: Live 20-minute run: orchestrator drove tmux panes, built a pitch-roasting app, made a video, drafted and sent X DMs.
tools.quote: we're going to give it a task and build a product. So, it's going to use ECC skills
tools.check: Star count (271k) and exit claims are the guest's; X DM step needs private context and credentials.
